description: We build an intuitive web app for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge: compare south-pole landing sites and dates in seconds, showing when a site is lit and when Earth is visible for communication. Built on real ephemeris data so every number is checkable, with plain-language explanations for planners, educators and the public. Our team has hackathon experience in data dashboards and AI tools and is aiming for a polished, working demo.
summary:
L.U.N.A. (Lunar Understanding Navigator and Analysis) is an interactive platform for exploring and assessing potential lunar landing sites. It brings together real lunar topographic data, solar-visibility analysis, terrain assessment, and immersive 3D visualization to make the trade-offs of landing-site selection easier to understand.

Users can investigate lunar regions through interactive topographic, solar, and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) connection maps. The platform provides insight into elevation, slope, surface characteristics, and other terrain factors that can affect landing safety and mission planning.

Solar visibility is a core part of L.U.N.A. Understanding when the Sun is visible, or blocked by nearby terrain, is essential for evaluating illumination conditions and the likely availability of solar power during a mission. By connecting local terrain with sunlight and communication availability, L.U.N.A. helps users identify the practical advantages and constraints of possible landing locations.

L.U.N.A. also includes a fully functioning demo and an integrated tutorial that introduces users to the platform’s tools and workflows. The guided experience makes exploration intuitive, helping users quickly understand the maps, terrain analysis, and site-assessment features without requiring prior expertise.
details:
L.U.N.A. – Lunar Understanding Navigator and Analysis

Project Overview

L.U.N.A. is a browser-based lunar exploration and landing-site assessment platform designed to help users understand how terrain and solar illumination influence potential landing locations.

Rather than presenting lunar terrain as a static map, our platform combines multiple complementary capabilities: topographic analysis, solar visibility assessment, and DTE connection.

To make these masks easier to interpret, we built a fully functional demo and guided tutorial that familiarizes users with the system and helps develop intuition for its analysis tools.

Solar Visibility Analysis

A central feature of L.U.N.A. is the investigation of solar visibility at selected locations on the Moon.

The surrounding topography can obstruct the Sun, producing extended periods of shadow that may affect solar-powered equipment and surface operations. This is especially relevant in polar regions, where the Sun remains close to the horizon.

Our project aims to make these illumination constraints understandable through interactive visualization and location-specific analysis.

Solar visibility is therefore treated as a fundamental landing-site consideration rather than an isolated visualization feature.

Topographic Analysis

Users can inspect lunar elevation data, examine terrain profiles, identify steep slopes, and compare surface characteristics across different locations.

The platform provides preliminary terrain-risk indicators based on elevation differences, slope, and estimated surface roughness.

Immersive Lunar Exploration

Users can select a location on a topographic map and explore the corresponding terrain in a 200 by 200km 3D Slice of the Moons Surface,

Terrain, Sun and Radio visualization provide an intuitive sense of the terrain's scale, relief, shadows and the navigational challenges.

Innovation and Intended Impact

The distinguishing concept behind L.U.N.A. is the integration of scientific analysis and interactive exploration.

The platform brings together the questions:

  • Where could a spacecraft land?
  • How challenging is the surrounding terrain?
  • When is the Sun visible at that location?
  • How might illumination constraints affect mission planning?
  • How does the communication with Earth work at the site?

With the help of NASA Databases (LOLA, JPL Horizons) L.U.N.A. makes lunar landing-site analysis more accessible to students, researchers, and space enthusiasts while demonstrating how NASA-derived data can support exploration and mission-planning decisions.
